review_notes: I read the whole target file and the WithAbs ring file (Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/WithAbs.lean). The toAbs/ofAbs simp lemmas for add, mul, sub, neg, pow, div and inv are already present and consistent. I also checked the downstream uses in NumberTheory/NumberField/Completion/InfinitePlace.lean and Analysis/AbsoluteValue/Equivalence.lean. I did not run Lean. Whether the proposed simp lemmas would cause conflicts or loops is not verified. The first finding suggests only a modest, hedged improvement.

findings.excerpt:
theorem algebraMap_apply (x : v.Completion) :
    algebraMap v.Completion w.Completion x = UniformSpace.Completion.mapRingHom
findings.problem: The file exposes the algebra structure on completions only through `algebraMap_eq` and `algebraMap_apply`. Both are non-simp unfoldings into `mapRingHom`, and `algebraMap_apply` is just `congrFun` of `algebraMap_eq`. The normal form simp needs is the action on embedded elements: `algebraMap v.Completion w.Completion (↑(toAbs v k)) = ↑(toAbs w (algebraMap K L k))`. No such general simp lemma exists here. Downstream, `NumberField.InfinitePlace.Completion` has to add its own `@[simp] algebraMap_coe`, specialised to number fields. The same normal form is missing for every other user of `algebraOfLiesOver`.
findings.proposed_change: Add a general `@[simp]` lemma next to `algebraMap_eq`. It would state `algebraMap v.Completion w.Completion (x : WithAbs v) = ((WithAbs.map v w (algebraMap K L) x : WithAbs w) : w.Completion)`. The proof would use `UniformSpace.Completion.mapRingHom_coe` after `rw [algebraMap_eq]`. Optionally add a `K`-level version for `↑k`. Keep `algebraMap_eq` non-simp, since it unfolds into a less canonical form. Then check whether the `InfinitePlace` lemma `algebraMap_coe` can be derived from it or removed.
findings.benefit: Simp would reduce `algebraMap` on coerced elements to the coerced image in `WithAbs w`, which `WithAbs.map_apply` then normalises. Users would no longer need to `rw [algebraMap_eq]` and unfold `mapRingHom`, and each number-field or function-field development would not need its own specialised copy.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem algebraMap_coe (x : WithAbs v.1) :
    algebraMap v.Completion w.Completion x = algebraMap (WithAbs v.1) (WithAbs w.1) x

findings.declaration: WithAbs.isometry_map (use of norm_eq_apply_ofAbs); lemma defined in Ring/WithAbs.lean
findings.problem: The norm on `WithAbs v` is defeq to `v (ofAbs x)`, but `norm_eq_apply_ofAbs` and `norm_toAbs_eq` are not simp lemmas. The proof has to name `norm_eq_apply_ofAbs` in a `simp_rw` before the final `simp`. Other places do the same: `simpa [WithAbs.norm_eq_apply_ofAbs]` in InfinitePlace.lean and in Equivalence.lean. So plain `simp` cannot reduce `‖x‖` or `‖toAbs v x‖` to the absolute value, and the interface has no canonical form for norms in `WithAbs v`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `WithAbs.norm_toAbs_eq` as `@[simp]`. Its LHS has the head `toAbs`, so it is specific to `WithAbs` and does not clash with generic norm lemmas. Consider also `@[simp]` on `norm_eq_apply_ofAbs`, since its LHS is a norm on `WithAbs v` only. Then `isometry_map` would reduce to `simp [map_apply, AbsoluteValue.under_def]` with no explicit norm rewrite. Check that this does not conflict with other simp lemmas for `‖·‖` on `WithAbs` instances.
findings.benefit: Simp-set users get a uniform normal form (`v x`) and no longer need to remember `WithAbs.norm_eq_apply_ofAbs`. The `simp_rw`/`simpa [..]` workarounds in this file and in the other files that cite the lemma can be shortened.

evidence.excerpt: lemma norm_eq_apply_ofAbs (v : AbsoluteValue R ℝ) (x : WithAbs v) : ‖x‖ = v x.ofAbs := rfl
